faqs.question: What is the INVENIO FT-IR Research Spectrometer used for?
faqs.answer: The INVENIO is a modular research-grade FT-IR platform, used across pharmaceutical R&D, polymer science, chemistry, materials research, and semiconductor development.

faqs.question: What makes the INVENIO different from a routine FT-IR spectrometer?
faqs.answer: Every core feature can be upgraded in the field at any time, and the solution supports up to seven software-controlled detectors, covering the full spectral range from 28,000 to 15 cm⁻¹ in a single automated measurement.

faqs.question: What is the spectral resolution of the INVENIO?
faqs.answer: Below 0.085 cm⁻¹, suited to research requiring fine spectral detail.

faqs.question: Can the INVENIO run two experiments at once?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Transit channel is an independent second measurement channel with its own detector, running alongside the main sample compartment.

faqs.question: Can the INVENIO be upgraded after purchase?
faqs.answer: Yes. All core features can be added or changed in the field at any time, as research requirements evolve.

faqs.question: What extensions are available for the INVENIO?
faqs.answer: FT-IR microscopy with HYPERION II, FT-Raman with RAM II, thermogravimetric coupling, high-throughput screening with HTS-XT, and EMILIE for picogram-level nanomaterial analysis.

faqs.question: Is the INVENIO suitable for regulated pharmaceutical work?
faqs.answer: Yes. OPUS software complies with major pharmacopeia requirements and 21 CFR Part 11, with secure data handling for data integrity.

faqs.question: What is EMILIE?
faqs.answer: EMILIE is a nanomechanical infrared analyzer that integrates with the INVENIO for picogram-level sensitivity on nanomaterials, aerosols, and trace-level samples, without cryogenic cooling.

faqs.question: What is time-resolved spectroscopy used for on the INVENIO?
faqs.answer: It supports kinetics studies and reaction monitoring down to the nanosecond timescale, useful for researching catalysts and batteries under real-world conditions.

faqs.question: What is the price of the INVENIO FT-IR Research Spectrometer in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on the detector configuration, interferometer, and extensions your research needs. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the INVENIO FT-IR Research Spectrometer in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Bruker INVENIO FT-IR Research Spectrometer in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

body: The INVENIO isn't sized for one job. It's sized for whichever job you bring to it, and reconfigured when the next one is different.

Detector capacity is built in layers: the DigiTect slot for a detector of choice, such as an LN2-cooled option, the MultiTect unit adding up to five more room-temperature or thermostabilized detectors, and the Transit channel's own independent detector for a second experimental setup. Together, that's up to seven software-controlled detectors on one solution. Pair the MultiTect with the upgraded INTEGRAL interferometer, and the full spectral range, 28,000 down to 15 cm⁻¹, runs as a single automated measurement.

faqs.question: What is the VERTEX 80/80v FT-IR Research Spectrometer used for?
faqs.answer: It's a peak-performance research FT-IR platform used across semiconductor research, pharmaceutical analysis, physics, and surface science, wherever the highest resolution or sensitivity is required.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the VERTEX 80 and VERTEX 80v?
faqs.answer: The VERTEX 80v adds an evacuated optics bench, removing atmospheric moisture from the beam path. This enables high-resolution work, ultra-fast rapidscan, step-scan, and UV-range measurements that the standard purge-optics VERTEX 80 doesn't reach.

faqs.question: What resolution can the VERTEX 80/80v achieve?
faqs.answer: Standard configuration reaches better than 0.2 cm⁻¹. The PEAK configuration reaches better than 0.06 cm⁻¹, which Bruker states is the highest resolution achieved on a commercial benchtop FT-IR spectrometer.

faqs.question: What spectral range does it cover?
faqs.answer: From 50,000 cm⁻¹ in the UV/VIS region down to 5 cm⁻¹ in the far IR and terahertz range, the broadest range in Bruker's benchtop FT-IR line.

faqs.question: Can external light sources and accessories be connected?
faqs.answer: Yes. Five exit ports and two input ports allow simultaneous connection of accessories such as synchrotron sources, bolometers, FT-IR microscopes, and Raman modules.

faqs.question: Can beamsplitters be changed without opening the instrument?
faqs.answer: Yes, on the VERTEX 80v. The BMS-c option remotely exchanges up to four beamsplitter types automatically, under vacuum, without venting the optics bench.

faqs.question: Is the VERTEX 80/80v suitable for nanoscience research?
faqs.answer: Yes. The evacuated VERTEX 80v reaches sensitivity below 10⁻³ monolayers, suited to demanding surface and nanomaterial studies.

faqs.question: Can it be used for terahertz spectroscopy?
faqs.answer: Yes. A broadband far IR/THz beamsplitter covers approximately 900 down to 5 cm⁻¹ in a single measurement, and an external Hg-arc source with a room-temperature DTGS detector makes the terahertz range accessible.

faqs.question: What is EMILIE, and does it work with this solution?
faqs.answer: EMILIE is a nanomechanical infrared analyzer that adds picogram-level sensitivity for nanomaterials and trace-level samples, without cryogenic cooling. It's compatible with the VERTEX 80/80v.

sections.title: Resolution, Vacuum Optics and Spectral Range
body: Two decisions shape which VERTEX configuration fits your work: how much resolution you need, and whether atmospheric moisture can be allowed anywhere near your measurement.

The standard VERTEX 80 reaches better than 0.2 cm⁻¹, sufficient for most ambient-pressure gas-phase studies and room-temperature sample work. The PEAK configuration pushes that to better than 0.06 cm⁻¹, useful for low-temperature crystalline semiconductor work or gas-phase measurements at reduced pressure. The VERTEX 80v goes a step further, evacuating the entire optics bench so atmospheric water vapour cannot mask weak spectral features, which is what makes nanoscience work down to below 10⁻³ monolayers possible.

Standard resolution runs better than 0.2 cm⁻¹. The PEAK configuration reaches better than 0.06 cm⁻¹, which Bruker states is the highest resolution achieved on a commercial benchtop FT-IR spectrometer.

products.overview: A thermal analyzer tells you a sample lost weight, and at what temperature. It doesn't tell you what left. TG-FTIR couples the two techniques together: thermogravimetric analysis quantifies the mass change, and FT-IR spectroscopy identifies the gases released, at the moment they're released. Every substance except homonuclear diatomics and noble gases gives a characteristic infrared spectrum, which is what makes the identification possible. Three coupling methods connect the two systems, chosen for your flexibility, sensitivity, or setup requirements, and one of them, PERSEUS, links directly to the ALPHA II, with no transfer line at all.

faqs.question: What is TG-FTIR?
faqs.answer: TG-FTIR couples thermogravimetric analysis with FT-IR spectroscopy, so the mass change a sample undergoes and the identity of the gases it releases are measured together, also known as Hyphenated FT-IR or Evolved Gas Analysis.

faqs.question: Why can't thermal analysis alone identify the gases released?
faqs.answer: Thermogravimetric analysis measures mass change accurately, but it has no way to identify what left the sample. FT-IR spectroscopy adds that identification, since nearly every substance produces a characteristic infrared spectrum.

faqs.question: What are the three coupling modes?
faqs.answer: External coupling, using an external gas cell and transfer line for maximum FT-IR flexibility; internal coupling, using the FT-IR's own sample chamber; and PERSEUS, a direct connection with no transfer line, pairing the ALPHA II with a NETZSCH Thermoanalyzer.

faqs.question: What is PERSEUS?
faqs.answer: PERSEUS is a patented direct coupling between the compact ALPHA II FT-IR spectrometer and NETZSCH Thermoanalyzers, with no transfer line required.

faqs.question: Which detector should I choose for external coupling?
faqs.answer: A room-temperature DLaTGS detector suits routine sensitivity needs. A liquid-nitrogen-cooled MCT detector offers higher sensitivity for trace-level evolved gases.

faqs.question: What controls detection sensitivity in TG-FTIR?
faqs.answer: Sensitivity follows Beer's law: it depends on the cell's path length, the cell's volume, and the molecule's own absorptivity, which cannot be changed by the experimental setup.

faqs.question: Are there substances FT-IR cannot detect?
faqs.answer: Yes. Homonuclear diatomics and noble gases do not produce an infrared spectrum, since their vibration does not change the molecule's dipole moment.

faqs.question: What applications has TG-FTIR been used for?
faqs.answer: Documented studies include plasticizer analysis, aspirin decomposition, PUR powder coating identification, potassium acetate and HNF decomposition, and PVC cable coating failure analysis.

faqs.question: Does TG-FTIR include the thermal analyzer?
faqs.answer: No. TG-FTIR is a coupling technique; the thermal analyzer and the Bruker FT-IR spectrometer are separate components, and Inkarp confirms the right pairing for your work.

faqs.question: What is the price of TG-FTIR coupling in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your thermal analyzer, the FT-IR spectrometer chosen, and the coupling mode required. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your configuration is confirmed.

faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for Bruker TG-FTIR Thermogravimetric Analysis FT-IR Research Spectrometers in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

sections.title: Coupling Modes and Detection Sensitivity
body: Choosing a coupling mode is really choosing what you're prepared to trade for flexibility, sensitivity, or simplicity.

External coupling gives the most flexibility, since the FT-IR system stays free to run standalone measurements and switches to combined TG-FT-IR runs on command, with a detector choice of room-temperature DLaTGS or a more sensitive liquid-nitrogen-cooled MCT. Internal coupling uses the FT-IR's own sample chamber, and its sensitivity is governed directly by Beer's law: a longer cell path length passes more molecules at any given moment, while a smaller cell volume concentrates the same evolved gas more strongly, both raising the signal. PERSEUS removes the transfer line entirely, pairing the ALPHA II directly with a NETZSCH Thermoanalyzer.
